key_insight: A simple one-shot probe can reveal whether a vision-language foundation model's pretraining data underrepresents a niche domain or concept, without needing labeled test sets from that domain. This enables quick, low-cost auditing of VLFM coverage using a single exemplar and similarity statistics.
problem_solved: Lack of labeled test data and practical techniques to assess whether foundation models (e.g., CLIP) learned or underrepresent specialised, novel, or Global South domains from their pretraining data.
method: One-shot exemplar: pick a single representative image/text pair from the target domain as the probe.
Embed & compare: compute VLFM image/text embeddings for the probe and a large unlabeled corpus or retrieval set, then measure similarity distributions and retrieval ranks.
Score & decide: contrast similarity/rank statistics against reference classes or calibrated thresholds to flag underrepresentation (optionally with prompt ensembling and controls).
impact: Provides a lightweight, scalable tool for researchers and practitioners to audit pretraining coverage and identify domains needing targeted data collection, fine-tuning, or fairness interventions—especially useful when labelled evaluation sets are unavailable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: single exemplar -> embedding with VLFM -> retrieval/similarity analysis -> underrepresentation flag
Bar chart or violin plots comparing similarity distributions for target domain vs. reference domains (shows shift/lower scores)
Heatmap or t-SNE of embeddings illustrating clustering (target exemplar far from expected cluster indicates underrepresentation)
Icon set: globe/Global South, magnifying glass (audit), single sample (one-shot), and warning/flag (underrepresented)
paper_title: Underrepresented in Foundation Model Pretraining Data? A One-Shot Probe
paper_authors: Chris Vorster, Mayug Maniparambil, Noel E. O'Connor, Noel Murphy, Derek Molloy
